questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. We bought / two dozens / mangoes from / the market.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

We bought / two dozens / mangoes from / the market.
questions.solution: In the given sentence, 'two dozen' should be used instead of 'two dozens'. We never write ‘dozens’ if we are using a numerical amount like two, three, etc. before it. Similarly, the given sentence has ‘two’ as a numerical value.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. You shall repented tomorrow for your misdeeds.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

You shall repented tomorrow for your misdeeds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the phrase 'shall repented' is incorrect.
  • The correct form should be 'shall repent' to match the future tense.
  • The word 'shall' is a modal verb that should be followed by the base form of the main verb, which is 'repent' in this case.
    • Example: You  shall repent tomorrow for your misdeeds.

Hence the correct statement is You shall repent tomorrow for your misdeeds.

Additional Information

  • Modal verbs like shall, will, can, could, may, might, must, ought to, should, would are always followed by the base form of the main verb.
    • Example: She can swim very well.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Raju was / a little boy / who were born / in a poor family.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Raju was / a little boy / who were born / in a poor family.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: who were born

Key Points

  • The error here lies in the subject-verb agreement.
  • The basic rule states that a singular subject takes a singular verb while a plural subject takes a plural verb.
  • Raju is a third-person singular subject.
  • In the first case "was" is used for a singular subject which is perfectly fine.
  • We use "who" in the sentence to replace the noun. ('Raju' in this sentence)
  • So, we must use "was" (singular verb) in the second case.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4, which contains an error.

Corrected sentence: Raju was a little boy who was born in a poor family.

questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I wish / I am / the Principal / of the school!
questions.solution: The part 'I am' contains an error. It should be replaced by 'I were'. The subjunctive mood is the verb form used to explore a hypothetical situation.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. There’s an quiet street down the left that you can use for your dance practice.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

There’s an quiet street down the left that you can use for your dance practice.
questions.solution: The correct answer: There’s an quiet street  Explanation: The correct article before a word starting with a consonant sound is "a," not "an." Therefore, it should be "a quiet street" instead of "an quiet street."

questions.question: Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. She will come to work though it doesn’t rain tomorrow.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

She will come to work though it doesn’t rain tomorrow.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'though it doesn't'.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the conjunction 'though' is incorrect.
  • The conjunction 'though' means despite the fact that; although.
  • The conjunction 'if' should be used in place of 'though'.
  • The conjunction 'if' is used for introducing a conditional clause on the condition or supposition that; in the event that.


Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Sentence: She will come to work if it doesn’t rain tomorrow.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The Prime Minister, along with the other ministers have left for America.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The Prime Minister, along with the other ministers have left for America.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. have left

As a rule, when a sentence refers to 2 subjects, the verbs in the sentence should refer to the subject that comes first. Here it is 'the Prime Minister' and he is a singular entity, thus the verbs should also be singular. Thus, 'have' needs to be replaced with 'has'.

Thus, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Mr. Roy was not only very successful and humble also.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Mr. Roy was not only very successful and humble also.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is 'and humble also'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of correlative conjunction since it has not only in the first clause.
  • Correlative conjunctions are a pair of words that connect similar entities(nouns, adjectives, etc) in the sentence together.
  • It is used to put emphasis on certain elements.
  • Common examples of correlative conjunctions include either or, neither nor, not only but also, both and.

Hence the correct sentence is: Mr. Roy was not only very successful but also humble.

Additional Information

  • Correlative conjunction is also known to maintain the grammatical balance in a sentence.
  • it can only connect two similar entities together. Like if the first clause of the sentence had a noun then it will be connected to another noun in the second clause of the sentence.
    • Example: Both India and China have huge populations. (nouns)

Confusion Points

  • It is really easy to get confused about which conjunction to use in a particular sentence.
  • If the first clause of the statement is similar to the second clause then we can use coordinating conjunction like and.
    • Example: He was handsome and talented as well.
  • If the first clause of the statement is in stark contrast to the second clause of the statement then we use but.
    • Example: He was talented but lacked discipline.
  • There is no need to use commas in case two nouns are connected through conjunction but in other sentences a comma is necessary.
    • Example: The restaurant owner not only offered us a free lunch, but he also gave us a complimentary beverage.

questions.question: Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Either Ramesh or Reema have the keys to the cupboard.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Either Ramesh or Reema have the keys to the cupboard.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'or Reema have'.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the plural form of the verb 'have' is incorrect.
  • 'Ramesh' and 'Reema' are two singular nouns.
  • Two singular nouns connected by 'or' or 'nor' take a singular verb.
  • Therefore, the singular form of the verb 'has' should be used in place of the plural verb 'have'.


Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Sentence: Either Ramesh or Reema has the keys to the cupboard.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The blue is a beautiful colour.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The blue is a beautiful colour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • The word 'The' before 'blue' is unnecessary in the context of the given sentence.
  • In English, we generally do not use the definite article 'the' before colors unless we are referring to something specific that has already been mentioned or is known.
  • Therefore, the correct sentence should be: Blue is a beautiful colour.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1. 

Additional Information

  • Articles (a, an, the) are used before nouns to provide context. 'The' is a definite article used to refer to something specific.
  • When talking about colors in a general sense, we do not use the definite article 'the'.
    • Example: Red is a vibrant colour.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. Alaska in the USA / is the colder / of all the states.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Alaska in the USA / is the colder / of all the states.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect comparative form "colder" being used instead of the superlative form "coldest."
  • When comparing more than two entities, the superlative form of an adjective should be used.
  • The correct phrase should be "is the coldest of all the states," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 1 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "Alaska in the USA is the coldest of all the states."
 
Additional Information
  • Part 4: "Alaska in the USA" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • Part 2: "is the colder" – This part contains the error as explained above.
  • Part 3: "of all the states." – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • No error – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 2.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Either Avika or Nikunj are going to win the prize in the handwriting competition.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Either Avika or Nikunj are going to win the prize in the handwriting competition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'are going to'.

Key Points

  • Here, one must have a basic knowledge of correlative conjunction to check this type of question.
  • Whenever either... or is used, the verb has to agree with the noun, nearest to it.
    • ex: Either he or she cooks dinner.
    • ex: He either washes the clothes himself or asks her to wash them.

The corrected sentence will be like: Either Avika or Nikunj is going to win the prize in the handwriting competition.

Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The supermarket is open from 10 a.m. still 10 p.m.

The supermarket is open from 10 a.m. still 10 p.m.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: still 10 p.m.

The correct word should be "until" instead of "still" to indicate the time duration. The sentence should read: "The supermarket is open from 10 a.m. until 10 p.m."

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. He was (a) bad injured (b) in the (c) last match.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
He was (a) bad injured (b) in the (c) last match.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect usage of the word "bad" instead of "badly."

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She were singing / beautifully in / the concert hall / last night.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She were singing / beautifully in / the concert hall / last night.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: "She were singing." The correct form should be "She was singing" because "was" is the appropriate past tense of "to be" for the singular subject "She."

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. Ram cannot withdraw all his money unless he does not give a prior notice.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Ram cannot withdraw all his money unless he does not give a prior notice.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

'unless he does not give' is grammatically incorrect because 'unless' means except if.

Here, 'unless' and 'does not' are contrary to each other. So, it's wrong. 

Correct sentence: Ram cannot withdraw all his money if he does not give prior notice.

Additional Information

  • “if” is conditional. It is used to describe a possible situation, and what would happen under the conditions of that situation
    • For E.g.- "If you don't save some money, you can't go on vacation
  • “Unless” is also conditional, but it is effectively “if” with an extra exclusion or negative qualifier added
    • For e.g.- You can't go on vacation unless you save some money.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She received / an award / for her work / in a engineering field.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She received / an award / for her work / in a engineering field.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. in a engineering field.

Key Points

  • The given sentence has been divided into four segments:
    • She received
    • an award
    • for her work
    • in a engineering field
  • Segment 2, "in a engineering field", contains a grammatical error.
  • The article "a" is incorrect because it precedes the word "engineering," which begins with a vowel sound. The correct article in this context is "an."
  • The correct phrase should be "in an engineering field."

Correct sentence: She received an award for her work in an engineering field.

Additional Information

  • Usage of Articles:
    • "A": Used before words that begin with a consonant sound. Example: a book, a car.
    • "An": Used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Example: an apple, an engineer.
  • Common Errors:
    • Using the wrong article before a noun can make the sentence grammatically incorrect.
    • It is important to focus on the sound of the word that follows the article, not just the spelling.

questions.question: Directions: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. The publics are not satisfied with the new act.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

The publics are not satisfied with the new act.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The publics are' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the plural noun 'publics' and the plural verb 'are' is incorrect.
  • The noun 'public' is an uncountable noun or singular noun.
  • Therefore, the singular form of the noun 'public' should be used in place of the plural form 'publics'.
  • Also, we know that a singular noun or subject always takes a singular verb.
  • Therefore, the singular form of the verb 'is' should be used in place of the plural verb 'are'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence: The public is not satisfied with the new act.

Additional Information

  • Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number singular or plural.
  • If a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is a plural, its verb must also be plural.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He have / workers from / Ireland and France / in his factory.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He have / workers from / Ireland and France / in his factory.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: He have. The subject 'He' is third-person singular, requiring the singular verb 'has' instead of the plural 'have' to ensure proper subject-verb agreement.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. We hardly knew nothing / about the manager / who had recently joined.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

We hardly knew nothing / about the manager / who had recently joined.
questions.solution: The phrase "We hardly knew nothing" contains a double negative, which results in a grammatically incorrect construction. When "hardly" is used, it already implies a negative sense, so adding "nothing" creates redundancy. The corrected sentence, "We hardly knew anything about the manager who had recently joined," maintains clarity and proper grammatical structure.

questions.question: Identify the error in the given sentence. Ajit got to work earliest than everyone else today.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the error in the given sentence.
Ajit got to work earliest than everyone else today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. earliest than .

Key Points

  • The given sentence contains a grammatical error in the use of the word "earliest than".
  • The word "earliest" is the superlative form of the adjective "early," and it is not used with the word "than".
  • Instead, the comparative form "earlier" should be used when comparing two entities and is followed by "than."
  • Hence, the correct phrase should be "earlier than."

Correct sentence: Ajit got to work earlier than everyone else today.

Additional Information

  • Superlative adjectives: Used to describe the highest degree of a quality (e.g., earliest, fastest, tallest).
  • Comparative adjectives: Used to compare two entities (e.g., earlier, faster, taller).
  • In this sentence, since a comparison is being made between Ajit and everyone else, the comparative form "earlier" is appropriate.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. According to the encyclopaedia, a oasis is an area which is made fertile by a source of freshwater.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

According to the encyclopaedia, a oasis is an area which is made fertile by a source of freshwater.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Option 2. Explanation: "a oasis" is grammatically incorrect because "oasis" begins with a vowel sound and should be preceded by "an".

questions.solution: Replace "not" with "nor" to correct the sentence. 'Neither/nor' is used when two options are invalid. In the given sentence it is said that, 'she and I' are not participating in the debate tournament. (both are negative).

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Amla juice / is rich with / Vitamin C. / no error
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Amla juice / is rich with / Vitamin C. / no error
questions.solution: The correct answer is "is rich with". 'With' should be replaced by 'in'. Rich in (something) means having an abundance of something, especially some valuable resource other than money. Correct Sentence: Amla Juice is rich in Vitamin C.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. One of the boys from our school have been selected for National Badminton Championship
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

One of the boys from our school have been selected for National Badminton Championship
questions.solution:
The correct answer is have been selected

Key Points

  • 'has been selected' should be there in place of 'have been selected'
  • The 'one of' is a singular term and generally used to talk about a noun or a pronoun.
  • The noun or a pronoun used after the phrase “one of” is always in the plural form.
  • The helping verb will always be in the singular form, as the helping verb agrees with “one of” and not with the plural noun in the sentence.
    Example: One of the students was selected to visit NASA.
  • Thus, the correct sentence is: One of the boys from our school has been selected for National Badminton Championship

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I decided to / sang a song / in the interschool / song competition.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I decided to / sang a song / in the interschool / song competition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'sang a song', i.e. the error lies in this part of the sentence.

Key Points

  • The error lies in the incorrect usage of the infinitive.
  • Infinitive verb: An infinitive is the basic form of a verb, having no tense and not being conjugated. In English, an infinitive is preceded by the word 'to'.
  • Structure:
    • To + the first form of the verb
      • Example: to dance, to sing, to go, etc.
  • Thus, the usage of the second form of the verb with 'to' is incorrect.
  • It needs to be replaced with its first form of the verb, i.e. 'sing'.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.
     

Correct sentence: I decided to sing a song in the interschool song competition.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The Prime Minister and a President are visiting the town today to see the preparations of International Seminar.

The Prime Minister and a President are visiting the town today to see the preparations of International Seminar.

questions.solution: The correct answer: A President are visiting Explanation: The marked option is correct because "a President" should be "the President" to be grammatically consistent with "The Prime Minister" and indicate a specific person.

questions.question: From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. My sister tried to tempt me with sweets so that I ought not tell our parents about the vase she broke.
questions.questionHtml:
From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

My sister tried to tempt me with sweets so that I ought not tell our parents about the vase she broke.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (2). 'ought not tell'.

Key Points

  • 'ought not tell' is not grammatically correct.
  • The preposition 'to' is used with the modal verb 'ought' which expresses obligation or duty.
    • Example: We ought not to laugh at the poor boy.
    • Hence, 'to' should be used before the word 'tell'.
    • So, the correct answer is option 2).


Correct sentence: My sister tried to tempt me with sweets so that I ought not to tell our parents about the vase she broke.

questions.question: Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Laisha should holding / a meeting in the / Prem Auditorium / tomorrow evening.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Laisha should holding / a meeting in the / Prem Auditorium / tomorrow evening.
questions.solution: The error lies in the part "Laisha should holding." The verb 'should' does not require the -ing form of the verb that follows it. Structure: Subject + should + V1 + Object. "Holding" should be replaced with the base form of the verb 'hold.' Correct sentence: Laisha should hold a meeting in the Prem Auditorium tomorrow evening.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. A fox and an hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
A fox and an hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: and an hyena.

Key Points

  • The article "an" is used before words that start with a vowel sound, while "a" is used before words that start with a consonant sound.
  • In the given sentence, the word "hyena" starts with a consonant sound "h", so the correct article to use is "a".

Correct sentence: A fox and a hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.

Additional Information

  • Articles "a" and "an":
    • "A": Used before words that begin with a consonant sound. Example: a car, a university.
    • "An": Used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Example: an apple, an hour.
  • Common Mistakes:
    • Incorrect: an university (since "university" starts with a consonant sound).
    • Correct: a university.

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. She ran so fastly that I could not overtake her. /No error
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

She ran so fastly that I could not overtake her. /No error
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

'She ran so fastly' is wrong in the given sentence because 'fastly' is an adverb.

An adverb is a word or phrase that modifies or qualifies an adjective, verb, or other adverb or a word group, expressing a relation of place, time, circumstance, manner, cause, degree, etc.

Here, in the given sentence 'fastly' doesn't qualify anything. So, it is grammatically wrong.

Instead, the word fast should be used.

Correct Sentence : She ran so fast that I could not overtake her.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Tushar is junior than all his colleagues.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Tushar is junior than all his colleagues.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • In the first part of the given sentence, the comparative form 'junior than' is incorrect.
  • The correct usage should be 'junior to' instead of 'junior than'.
  • In English, words like junior, senior, superior, inferior, prefer etc., are followed by 'to' rather than 'than'.
  • Therefore, the correct form should be 'junior to'.

Hence, the correct statement is 'Tushar is junior to all his colleagues.'

Additional Information

  • When using comparative adjectives like junior, senior, superior, inferior, prefer, they are always followed by 'to' instead of 'than'.
    • Example: She is senior to me in the company.

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'. Vijay and Ajay is here to celebrate 7 years of their friendship.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Vijay and Ajay is here to celebrate 7 years of their friendship.
questions.solution: In the original sentence, there is a subject-verb agreement error. The subject "Vijay and Ajay" is plural, so the verb should also be in the plural form "are" instead of the singular form "is." The correct sentence is: 'Vijay and Ajay are here to celebrate 7 years of their friendship'.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: They secret. The adjective "secret" incorrectly modifies the verb "decided." It should be the adverb "secretly" to describe how they decided to leave.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. If the sentence has no error, then select 'No error'. How many money did Sudhir win in the lottery?
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. If the sentence has no error, then select 'No error'.

How many money did Sudhir win in the lottery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. How many money.

Key Points

  • The error is in the first segment of the sentence and it has to be modified.
  • The wrong determiner ‘many’ is used here. 
  • We can only use ‘many’ before countable nouns. Eg: How many dresses are available?
  • Money is an uncountable noun. We cannot say one money, two money etc. although it is possible to say one dollar or two rupees etc.
  • Hence we have to use the determiner ‘much’ which is always followed by an uncountable noun. Eg: How much time is left?
  • Hence the phrase “How many money” should be replaced with “How much money”.

Correct sentence: How much money did Sudhir win in the lottery?

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. My brother brought a few rice while coming from the market.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

My brother brought a few rice while coming from the market.
questions.solution: Rice is an uncountable noun. We can say 'a little rice' / 'some rice' or it can be written as 'a few grains of rice'. However, 'few' is a determiner used for countable nouns. Correct sentence: My brother brought a little / some rice while coming from the market.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He told / his senior, "I / will sung a song / at the party tonight."
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
He told / his senior, "I / will sung a song / at the party tonight."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. will sung a song .

Key Points

  • The error is in the segment "will sung a song." The verb "sung" is the past participle form and is incorrectly used here.
  • When using the simple future tense, the correct structure is "will" followed by the base form of the verb ("sing" in this case).

Correct sentence: He told his senior, "I will sing a song at the party tonight."

Additional Information

  • Simple Future Tense Structure:
    • Structure: Subject + will/shall + base verb.
    • Example: She will call you tomorrow.
    • Usage: Describes actions that will happen in the future.

In the summer, the weathering can be very hot around here.
questions.solution: The error lies in the part "weathering" of the sentence. "Weather can be" is the correct phrase to use to describe the temperature in a particular location during the summer season. "Weathering" refers to the process of wearing away or breaking down due to exposure to the elements, and is not applicable in this context. So, we must replace "Weathering" with "Weather." Correct sentence: In the summer, the weather can be very hot around here.

  • The primary issue in the sentence is the use of "will" instead of "was" in the segment "will a heavy downpour."

  • In the given sentence, the superlative form of the adjective 'oldest' should be used instead of 'eldest'.

Additional Information

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. I am believing you have submitted all the necessary documents.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

I am believing you have submitted all the necessary documents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Option 4". 

Key Points

  • The sentence uses the verb "to believe" in its present continuous form ("I am believing"), which is not typically used in English for state verbs.
  • State verbs describe a state rather than an action and usually do not have continuous forms.
  • Verbs of perception, emotion, and thinking (such as "believe") are generally not used in the continuous form because they do not describe physical actions.
  • The correct form of the verb "to believe" in this context is the simple present tense ("I believe") because it expresses a general opinion or conviction.
  • Changing "I am believing" to "I believe" corrects the grammatical error, making the sentence "I believe you have submitted all the necessary documents."
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Much villagers attended the feast hosted by the village panchayat.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Much villagers attended the feast hosted by the village panchayat.
questions.solution:
The error is in 'Much villagers' 

Key Points
  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect and has an error of determiners.
  • Here 'Many villagers' should be used instead of 'Much villagers'
  • 'Much' is uncountable.
    • Example: There is too much food at home for us. { here we cannot count food }
  • 'Many' is countable.
    • ​Example: There are many girls in the classroom.{ here we can count girls }​

The correct sentence will be: 'Many' villagers attended the fest hosted by the village panchayat. 

  • Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

 

 Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत है और इसमें 'determiners ' की ​ त्रुटि है I
  • यहां 'Much villagers' के बजाय 'Many villagers' इस्तेमाल किया जाना चाहिए I
  • 'Much' अगणनीय है।
    • उदाहरण: There is too much food at home for us. { यहाँ हम भोजन की गिनती नहीं कर सकते }
  • 'Many' गणनीय है I
    • उदाहरण: There are many girls in the classroom.{ यहाँ हम लड़कियों की गिनती कर सकते हैं }

सही वाक्य होगा: 'Many' villagers attended the fest hosted by the village panchayat. 

  • अत: विकल्प 3 सही उत्तर है।

Confusion Points 

In the given sentence, the word "hosted" is functioning as a past participle, which acts as an adjective modifying the noun "fest." In this case, there is no need to include "was/were" before "hosted" because the sentence is in the active voice and the verb "hosted" is describing the fest.

If we were to rephrase the sentence using the passive voice, we could say: "The fest, which was hosted by the village panchayat, was attended by many villagers."

In this revised sentence, "was hosted" is used to indicate the passive voice, and the verb "attended" is in the past tense to match the verb tense of "was hosted."

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. My brother, who live in Delhi, has written me a letter.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

My brother, who live in Delhi, has written me a letter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is who live in Delhi.

Key Points

  • 'who lives in Delhi' should be there in place of 'who live in Delhi'
  • A relative pronoun (“who,” “which,” or “that”) used as a subject of an adjective clause takes either a singular or plural verb in order to agree with its antecedent.
    Example: 
    • A vegetable that contains DDT can be harmful. (Adjective clause modifying the singular noun “vegetable.”)
    • Vegetables that contain DDT can be harmful. (Adjective clause modifying the plural noun “vegetables.”) 
  • ​Here, 'my brother' is a singular subject, so a singular verb should be used.

Thus, the rectified sentence is: My brother, who lives in Delhi, has written me a letter.
